problems.stem: A team copies its Blackboard module structure verbatim into ALGET and calls the migration 'aligned.' What is the strongest correction?
options: It is aligned; everything was moved successfully.
Copying is not aligning; build an objective-to-activity table and check each objective has a matching ALGET activity.
Alignment just means the links open in ALGET.
Alignment means the modules appear in the same order.
problems.explanation: Alignment is the mapping of objectives to activities, not the reproduction of the old structure.

problems.stem: The migrated quiz has 10 recall items, all measuring Objective 1 (define terms). Objectives 2 to 4 ask students to analyze, document, and decide. What does the alignment table reveal?
options: All four objectives are covered because there are ten items.
Three objectives have no aligned activity; recall items cannot measure a design decision.
The quiz is fine because recall is the foundation.
problems.explanation: Recall items cannot show analysis, documentation, or decision; those objective cells are empty.

problems.stem: An instructor uses AI to suggest which ALGET feature serves each objective. What is the strongest boundary?
options: Adopt the AI mapping without checking it.
Use the AI suggestions, then verify each objective truly maps to a feature that can show that skill, leaving no orphaned activity.
Avoid AI and copy the Blackboard structure as-is.
Ask AI only to rename the activities.
problems.explanation: AI can propose mappings, but the instructor must confirm each objective is covered and no activity is orphaned.

problems.stem: Why replace the single-file storyboard dropbox with an artifact-studio before/after trace during migration?
options: The trace makes the gradebook simpler.
The dropbox captures only a finished file, so ALGET's adaptive support has no process evidence to act on.
A trace looks more modern than a dropbox.
problems.explanation: Adaptive support needs process evidence; a single-file upload records completion but no decision trail.
